table.name: conductor
table.purpose: A registry of conductors, one row per conductor, with their country and a reference to an orchestra (or similar grouping) they are associated with.

col_001.name: conductor_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate identifier for each conductor.

col_002.name: conductor_name
col_002.description: Full name of the conductor (e.g. Antal Doráti, Pierre Boulez). Unique per row.

col_003.name: orchestra_id
col_003.description: Foreign key to the orchestra table; the orchestra the conductor is associated with. Values cluster in the 40s, matching orchestra ids.

col_004.name: country
col_004.description: Country of the conductor (USA, UK, France).

table.name: orchestra
table.purpose: Catalog of orchestras, each row describing an orchestra along with metadata about a recording (record label, year, media format). Likely derived from a discography of orchestra recordings (e.g., classical music DVDs/CDs).

col_001.name: orchestra_id
col_001.description: Primary key; sequential integer identifier for each orchestra row (1-12).

col_002.name: orchestra_name
col_002.description: Full name of the orchestra (e.g., Chicago Symphony Orchestra, Kirov Orchestra).

col_003.name: orchestra_id_duplicate
col_003.description: Integer 1-12 that exactly mirrors col_001 in every sample row; appears to be a duplicate/redundant copy of the primary key, possibly a foreign key to itself or a leftover column. Its independent meaning is unresolved.

col_004.name: record_label
col_004.description: Name of the record label/publisher of the recording (Decca Records, Deutsche Grammophon, RCA, etc.).

col_006.name: media_format
col_006.description: Physical media format of the release: CD, DVD, or combined 'CD / LP'.

table.name: performance
table.purpose: Per-episode television ratings for a talent/competition show series (auditions, semi-finals, final): broadcast date, viewers, audience share, and weekly chart position. Likely scraped from a Wikipedia-style ratings table for a show in the 'show' table.

col_002.name: episode_number
col_002.description: Episode number within the series (1-11), matching col_001 one-to-one in this data. Could also be a foreign key to a show/episode table, but no joins were detected.

col_003.name: episode_title
col_003.description: Name of the episode/stage, e.g. 'Auditions 1'...'Auditions 5', 'Semi-final 3', 'Live final results', 'Series average'.

col_004.name: broadcast_date
col_004.description: Original air date, day and month only (e.g. '10 June'); year not stored. '17 June' appears twice, consistent with two episodes airing that day.

col_005.name: viewers_millions
col_005.description: Audience size in millions of viewers (5.2 to 11.58). The 'Series average' row value 11.45 suggests the average episode drew ~11.45m viewers.

col_006.name: weekly_rank
col_006.description: Position in the weekly TV ratings chart (stored as text; 'TBC' = to be confirmed). The '8' appearing twice likely reflects two episodes ranked 8th in different weeks.

col_007.name: audience_share
col_007.description: Share of total TV audience watching, as a percentage string (22.7%-43.7%).

table.name: stadium
table.purpose: A table of football stadiums (Scottish grounds: Hampden Park, Fir Park, St. Mirren Park, Glebe Park), one row per stadium, with capacity. The 'show'/'orchestra'/'conductor' table names appear to be misleading aliases for a football-related database.

col_001.name: stadium_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each stadium row.

col_003.name: stadium_name
col_003.description: Name of the stadium/venue (all are Scottish football grounds: Hampden Park, Fir Park, St. Mirren Park, Glebe Park).

col_005.name: capacity
col_005.description: Stadium capacity in number of seats/spectators. Values (555–2431) are small for real grounds, but the pattern of a per-venue integer with Glebe Park smallest and Hampden Park largest fits capacity; could also be some other per-stadium count.
